text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL GOV'T SAYS RE-ELECTION BILL'S PASSAGE ASSURED

The week began in crisis over President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's bid to get Congress to approve a re-election amendment ends in uncertainty despite renewed government assertions its passage is assured.
-- SALE OF PETROBRAS SHARES WILL BE FREED UP

A draft bill with regulations opening Brazil's oil sector allow foreign investors to buy and sell common shares of Petrobras and bars the state oil monopoly from directly distributing natural gas to large consumers.
-- NEW CPMF TAX PROMPTS LAUNCHING OF DEBENTURES

There is intense activity in the debentures market ahead of the imposition of Brazil's new CPMF tax on financial transactions as lead managers hurry issues to avoid the 0.2 percent levy due to take effect Jan 23.
O GLOBO
-- GOV'T PRESSURES ALLIES, SETS RE-ELECTION VOTE
The government has decided to confront its maverick ally, the PMDB party, and set a Jan 22 vote on its re-election amendment in Congress' lower house.
-- ORGAN DONATIONS NO LONGER WILL NEED FAMILY'S OK

President Fernando Henrique Cardoso is expected to sign a law in coming days allowing automatic organ donations, scrapping a requirement for family authorization. Only those who stipulate on their driver's license they do not want to be donors will be exempt.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- IMPASSE IN CONGRESS' LOWER HOUSE THREATENS RE-ELECTION

Brazil's government said it will ask the Chamber of Deputies to vote next week on a re-election amendment but the vote is being blocked by Congress' largest party, the PMDB, which wants it delayed until February.
-- TWO LANDLESS FARMERS SLAIN IN SOUTHERN BRAZIL

Two landless farmers were killed and one was seriously injured at a ranch in the southern state of Parana. Brazil's Landless Movement (MST) claimed they were ambushed by armed guards hired by the ranch while the ranch's owner speculated they were involved in an altercation with hunters.
-- PLANE CRASHES WITH BUSINESSMAN, FIVE OTHERS ABOARD

A twin-engine Cessna crashed yesterday in western Sao Paulo, killing all six people aboard, including shoe executive Vanderlei Silveira and his daughter. The wreckage was found hours after it crashed while en route from the town of Franca to Sao Paulo.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
